clue.text: Curly veg, if sound, consumed as religious rule

indicators.note: the word sound tells us the words before it are to be heard rather than spelt

parts.note: curly veg is kale, the crinkly-leaved cabbage; said with 'if' it gives the sound of a Muslim ruler's title
consumed means ate

explanation.surface: A dietary instruction: crinkly greens, if wholesome, eaten as a matter of religious law.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound' looks like an adjective meaning healthy, but it signals that KALE + IF is heard as CALIPH.
explanation.definitionFit: A caliphate is the rule or realm of a caliph, the Islamic religious and political leader.

clue.text: Vessel with some honey in crypt

parts.note: a cat is a catamaran or similar boat, a vessel
a comb of honey is a quantity of it

explanation.surface: A jar of honey left inside a crypt.
explanation.definitionFit: A catacomb is an underground burial chamber, much like a crypt beneath a church.

clue.text: Leah's dad gives dog a name

parts.note: a lab is a Labrador, a breed of dog

explanation.surface: A biblical father hands over his dog and gives it a name.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis Laban was the father of Leah and Rachel, both wives of Jacob.

clue.text: Always the same suit fabric? That's a 9

parts.note: perpetual means everlasting, always the same
check is a chequered cloth often used for suits

explanation.surface: A tailoring question about a suit cloth that never changes, followed by a comment on its hopelessness.
explanation.walkthrough: 9 is the answer to 9-down. In chess, endless checks force a draw, so neither side can win.
explanation.definitionFit: Perpetual check leads to a drawn game, an instance of a no-win situation for the stronger player.

clue.text: Killer I see reported going to block at Stonehenge for execution

indicators.note: going to means the second piece is attached after the first
execution means beheading, so the block loses its first letter

parts.note: sarsens are the great sandstone blocks of Stonehenge

indicators.note: reported means the words are as heard, giving a pair of letters with the same sound

parts.note: said aloud, the phrase I see is the same as the two letters I and C

explanation.surface: A murderer says he is heading to the stone at Stonehenge to be put to death.
explanation.walkthrough: Stonehenge is a prehistoric stone circle in Wiltshire, England.
explanation.definitionFit: Arsenic is a notorious poison, so it is a killer.

clue.text: Authorise me to return pawn, not so important after the opening

indicators.note: to return means the word me comes back reversed

parts.note: P is the chess abbreviation for pawn

indicators.note: after the opening means the first letter has gone

parts.note: lower means of less importance

explanation.surface: A chess player gives permission to take back a pawn which matters less once the opening is over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the opening' suggests the chess opening, but it means LOWER loses its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To empower someone is to give them the authority to act, so it is a synonym of authorise.

clue.text: Month, bleak and damp, turning summery?

indicators.note: turning tells us to read the joined pieces backwards

parts.note: raw weather is cold, bleak and damp

explanation.surface: A miserable chilly month suddenly turning into summer weather.
explanation.definitionFit: Summery weather is warm weather, so the two adjectives are synonyms here.

clue.text: How Wordsworth saw a crowd in a high-rise long ago

indicators.note: in a down answer rise means the word goes upward, reading backwards

parts.note: high means tall
once means at some time long ago

explanation.surface: A poet looking up at a throng in a tall building in the old days.
explanation.walkthrough: Wordsworth's daffodils poem runs 'When all at once I saw a crowd, A host, of golden daffodils'.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means suddenly, quoted from the line in which the poet catches sight of daffodils.

clue.text: See 23
3, for example, finally getting a job?

parts.note: now, as in 'now at last', can mean finally
getting in means arriving or being admitted
a situation is a post or job

explanation.surface: A job-seeker at last landing a position, given as an example.
explanation.walkthrough: 3 is the answer to 3-down, a chess draw by endless checking.
explanation.definitionFit: Perpetual check is a drawn position where neither player can win, an example of a hopeless predicament.

clue.text: Underground, is it? Or time to take a taxi?

parts.note: Uber is the ride-hailing taxi service

explanation.surface: Debating whether to travel by the London Underground or call a cab.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Underground' suggests the London Tube, but the definition is a potato-like growth that lives below ground.
explanation.definitionFit: A tuber, such as a potato, is a swollen stem growing below the soil, so it is literally underground.

clue.text: Serious writer's concession: a little comedy in the gaps

definitions.note: the 's stands for 'is', joining definition to wordplay

parts.note: a sop is a small concession made to placate someone

indicators.note: in places the small piece inside the gaps

parts.note: gaps are holes

indicators.note: a little of the word comedy is just its first letter

explanation.surface: A grave author admits that there is a touch of humour filling the gaps in the work.
explanation.definitionFit: Sophocles was the ancient Greek tragedian, the archetypal writer of serious drama.

clue.text: Is youngster fit for this culture at the Met?

parts.note: being fit or able to do something means you can
a teen is a youngster

explanation.surface: Asking whether a young person is suited to the culture at the Metropolitan Police or the Met opera.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Is youngster fit' reads as 'Can teen?'. The Met is London's Metropolitan Police; 'canteen culture' is the phrase for the macho attitudes of rank-and-file police officers.
explanation.definitionFit: Canteen culture is the informal, often prejudiced attitude among police officers, so the word completes that phrase.

clue.text: Gradually chip away tons in a space of time

indicators.note: in places the abbreviations inside the stretch of time

parts.note: a while is a space of time
T is the abbreviation for a ton, so two tons are TT

explanation.surface: Slowly working away at heavy loads over a period of time.
explanation.definitionFit: To whittle is to carve wood by shaving off bits, and figuratively to reduce something bit by bit.

clue.text: School being over, sister hugs Mark, college champion

indicators.note: over tells us the school word is turned back to front

parts.note: a gam is a school of whales

indicators.note: hugs means the sister wraps around what follows

parts.note: a nun is a religious sister
a scar is a mark on the skin
the LSE is the London School of Economics, a college of London University

explanation.surface: Term has ended, and a nun embraces a student called Mark, a college champion.
explanation.walkthrough: The theme is chess: Magnus Carlsen is the Norwegian world chess champion.
explanation.definitionFit: Magnus Carlsen held the world chess championship title, so he is a champion by example.

clue.text: Playing, I ought to win from the start, but give up

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters are moved around in play
the start of win is its first letter

explanation.surface: A player who should have won from the opening move ends up conceding.
explanation.definitionFit: To go without is to forgo or do without something, a synonym of giving it up.

clue.text: Going to get architect for nothing, making hard grind

indicators.note: to get signals the word Going acquiring a replacement
for marks the architect standing in place of the nothing

parts.note: O is zero, nothing
John Nash was the Regency architect of Regent Street and Buckingham Palace

explanation.surface: A builder is going to hire an architect for free, which will be hard work.
explanation.definitionFit: Gnashing describes grinding the teeth together hard, as in rage or pain.

clue.text: Goodness masking evil: example that may be handed to you on a plate

definitions.text: that may be handed to you on a plate

indicators.note: masking means the exclamation covers what it hides inside

parts.note: goodness and wow are both exclamations of surprise
ill can mean evil, as in ill will
a pattern is an example or model to copy

explanation.surface: A moral lesson about goodness hiding wickedness, offered to you ready-made.
explanation.walkthrough: 'handed to you on a plate' sounds like an idiom for something easy, but it is literal: the design printed on crockery.
explanation.definitionFit: Willow pattern is the classic blue-and-white Chinese-style design on china plates, so it comes on a plate.

clue.text: American native suggests a pseudonym for Eliot?

indicators.note: suggests means the pen-name is merely hinted at, its first word cut to an initial

parts.note: T. S. Eliot signed his cat poems as Old Possum

explanation.surface: A query whether a native American creature might give T. S. Eliot a pen name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old Possum's Book of Practical Cats' is Eliot's collection; O standing for Old makes O POSSUM.
explanation.definitionFit: The opossum is a marsupial found only in the Americas, so it is native there.

clue.text: A lot of beer consumes dole money in rough bar

indicators.note: consumes means the beer measure swallows what follows

parts.note: a pin is a small cask holding four and a half gallons of beer
a giro is a British unemployment benefit cheque

explanation.surface: Spending your benefits on beer in a seedy pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rough bar' looks like a pub but is a crude metal ingot.
explanation.definitionFit: Pig iron is crude iron cast from a blast furnace into rough bars called pigs.

clue.text: 4 the record, holding empty luggage out

parts.note: 4 is the answer to 4-down, whose chemical symbol is As

indicators.note: empty luggage has only its outer letters left

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: A cryptic note about a record with empty bags left out.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone sleeping is out cold, so out means unconscious here.

clue.text: Trumpeter's burst stomach

indicators.note: a burst stomach is broken apart, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A trumpet player has blown so hard that his stomach has ruptured.
explanation.definitionFit: Satchmo was the nickname of Louis Armstrong, the great jazz trumpet player.

clue.text: Country houses a small river flowing into a big one

indicators.note: flowing into describes the small river joining and entering the big one

parts.note: the Ganges is a great river of India
R is the abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: Stately homes set where a tributary runs into a mighty river.
explanation.definitionFit: A grange is a country house with farm buildings attached, so granges are country houses.

clue.text: Mad stranger turns out to be 14, for example

indicators.note: turns out suggests the letters are turned around into a new order

explanation.surface: An eccentric outsider is revealed to be a famous figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 14 is the answer to 14-across, the world chess champion.
explanation.definitionFit: Magnus Carlsen holds the top chess title, so he is an example of the highest-ranked player.

clue.text: Fitness fanatic making one change — one'll get rid of bad influences

definitions.text: one'll get rid of bad influences

indicators.note: making one change tells us to alter a single letter of the fitness word

parts.note: a fitness fanatic is a keen exerciser

explanation.surface: A gym enthusiast makes one change in life and expects to get rid of bad habits.
explanation.walkthrough: The one change turns the second E of EXERCISER into an O.
explanation.definitionFit: An exorciser drives out evil spirits, the bad influences of the definition.

clue.text: At start of intifada, gunmen question one Arab

indicators.note: the start of the word intifada is its first letter

parts.note: RA, the Royal Artillery, are gunners or gunmen
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: At the outbreak of a Palestinian uprising, armed men interrogate an Arab.
explanation.definitionFit: An Iraqi is a native of Iraq, an Arab country, so the noun is an example of an Arab.

clue.text: Spread a little butter on end of slice

parts.note: a pat is a small portion of butter

indicators.note: the end of slice is its last letter

explanation.surface: Instructions to spread a small knob of butter on the end of a slice of bread.
explanation.definitionFit: Pâté is a savoury paste spread on toast or bread, so it is a spread.

clue.text: Chief exec engages 14's predecessor to travel back with minimum staff

indicators.note: engages means the chief exec takes on, holding inside, the predecessor

parts.note: MD, managing director, is a chief executive
Viswanathan Anand was world chess champion before Magnus Carlsen

indicators.note: back says the travel word is read backwards

parts.note: to go is to travel

explanation.surface: A company boss hires a former champion to make a return trip with a skeleton crew.
explanation.definitionFit: A man-and-dog business is a tiny operation run by one person, so it describes minimal staffing.
